notes: Marker: self-predication with bố (father, Northern term; Southern: ba). tôi is neutral, but 'I am the father' is definitionally male.

text: Tôi là chồng của cô ấy.
notes: Marker: chồng (husband) predicated of the speaker — definitionally male.

text: Tôi là anh trai của Lan.
notes: Marker: anh trai (older brother) predicated of the speaker — definitionally male.

Marker: self-reference with anh (older-male 'I') while addressing the hearer as em; the standard self-introduction pattern of a male speaker. The Chào em opener forces the first-person reading of anh.

Marker: anh as first-person self-reference — the canonical 'I love you' from the male partner to a female/younger partner. Conventional reading is first person; out of context a third-person reading ('the older brother loves…') is theoretically possible.
Marker: mẹ (mother) predicated of the speaker — definitionally female.

text: Tôi là vợ của anh ấy.
notes: Marker: vợ (wife) predicated of the speaker — definitionally female.

text: Tôi là chị gái của Nam.
notes: Marker: chị gái (older sister) predicated of the speaker — definitionally female.
Marker: self-reference with chị (older-female 'I') while addressing the hearer as em; the standard self-introduction pattern of a female speaker.
tôi is the gender-neutral first-person pronoun; no other marker present.
Neutral tôi with no kinship self-reference; unmarked for speaker gender.
Impersonal statement; no person reference at all.
anh ấy (he) genders the third-person referent, not the speaker.

glossEn: My older brother is very tall.
notes: anh trai here is a noun for the referent (older brother); the speaker (tôi) can be any gender. The word anh must not be read as speaker self-reference.

glossEn: Are you well? (addressing an older woman)
notes: chị here is second person and genders the ADDRESSEE (an older female); the speaker's gender is unknown.
anh sits inside the quotation and marks the quoted speaker (Nam), not the narrator.
